title: Parish and Cipher
premise: Retired detective Silas Halloran, now barely keeping his bookshop afloat, is hired by a nervous stranger named Ada Voss to prove that her husband, a parish archivist, will not be murdered at the upcoming anniversary dinner — a murder she insists has not happened yet, though she describes it in unsettling detail. As Silas investigates, he discovers the 'prediction' matches three deaths he once solved off the books, all tied to a decades-old land deed hidden in the parish records. The killer is Ada's brother-in-law, the parish's beloved deacon, who has been erasing witnesses to the forged deed and knows every investigative move because he wrote the original case file Silas once relied on. At the anniversary dinner, Silas and Ada spring a trap using a falsified copy of the deed; the deacon confesses under the weight of his own recorded voice, and Silas must choose between turning him in and protecting Ada, who aided the cover-up of the first death. He chooses duty tempered by love: the deacon is arrested, Ada inherits the truth of her marriage, and Silas reopens the bookshop with its first honest ledger in years.
about_author: Theo Zhou is the pen name of a former court stenographer who spent fifteen years transcribing testimony before turning to fiction. They live above a secondhand bookshop and write mysteries about people who know too much.

chapters.title: The Weight of Unsold Books
chapters.summary: Silas Halloran closes another losing day at his bookshop, haunted by the three 'accidents' he quietly solved after retirement. POV: Silas. Emotional beat: restless purpose waiting for a spark.

chapters.title: A Client Who Pays for Nothing
chapters.summary: Ada Voss arrives with an envelope of cash, asking Silas to prove her husband won't be murdered at the parish anniversary dinner in six weeks. She describes the death in detail that chills him. POV: Silas. Emotional beat: dread disguised as curiosity.

chapters.title: The Anniversary Dinner
chapters.summary: Silas researches the annual St. Aldric's dinner, where parish elders toast their history. Ada's husband Thomas is the archivist preparing the guest list. POV: Ada. Emotional beat: love shadowed by certainty.

chapters.title: Three Accidents, One Pattern
chapters.summary: Silas revisits his old files: three deaths over nine years, each ruled accidental, each connected to St. Aldric's property records. His hands shake matching them to Ada's prediction. POV: Silas. Emotional beat: the past refusing burial.

chapters.title: The Deacon's Warm Welcome
chapters.summary: Silas visits the parish and meets Deacon Ambrose Fell, charming and helpful, who offers full access to the archives. Something in Fell's fluency about the old cases unsettles him. POV: Silas. Emotional beat: charm as camouflage.

chapters.title: What the Ledger Doesn't Say
chapters.summary: Ada secretly copies pages from Thomas's working notes, finding references to a land deed dated 1974 that appears in no official record. POV: Ada. Emotional beat: betrayal by paper.

chapters.title: The Bookshop Stakeout
chapters.summary: Someone searches Silas's shop at night, leaving books reordered with surgical precision. He recognizes the method: evidence handling from police procedure. POV: Silas. Emotional beat: being known too well.

chapters.title: Thomas Voss, Archivist
chapters.summary: Silas interviews Thomas under a false pretext, finding a meticulous man terrified of something he won't name, guarding a locked drawer. POV: Thomas. Emotional beat: fear wearing diligence.

chapters.title: The First Death, Retold
chapters.summary: Flashback chapter: nine years ago, Silas privately concluded that surveyor Edwin Marsh's fall was murder but lacked proof and let it go. POV: Silas. Emotional beat: guilt as sediment.

chapters.title: Dinner Invitations
chapters.summary: The guest list for the anniversary dinner circulates; Silas cross-references it against the dead and finds every surviving witness to the 1974 deed will be present. POV: Ada. Emotional beat: a trap laid in plain sight.

chapters.title: Fell Knows My Name
chapters.summary: Deacon Fell quotes Silas's own retired-case reasoning back to him verbatim, revealing access to sealed notes only one person could have written. POV: Silas. Emotional beat: the floor tilting.

chapters.title: The Case File Ghost
chapters.summary: Silas discovers the original investigating officer on Marsh's death was a young Ambrose Fell, before ordination. The hunter was always inside the file. POV: Silas. Emotional beat: vertigo of realization.

chapters.title: Ada's Marriage, Audited
chapters.summary: Ada confronts what Thomas hides: he discovered the forged deed months ago and has been quietly negotiating with someone. POV: Ada. Emotional beat: love interrogating loyalty.

chapters.title: The Locked Drawer
chapters.summary: Thomas shows Silas his evidence: photographs of the 1974 deed proving the parish land was stolen from a dissolved trust, enriching three founding families. POV: Thomas. Emotional beat: relief and terror together.

chapters.title: Second Death, Reopened
chapters.summary: Silas exhumes the second accident — notary Ruth Calloway's drowning — and finds Fell signed her paperwork the week before. POV: Silas. Emotional beat: cold clarity.

chapters.title: An Offer of Silence
chapters.summary: Fell visits the bookshop openly, offering to fund it generously if Silas takes a holiday through the dinner. The threat is wrapped in kindness. POV: Silas. Emotional beat: corruption's gentle face.

chapters.title: What Ada Withheld
chapters.summary: Silas learns Ada's family name appears among the trust beneficiaries — she may have hired him to protect her inheritance, not her husband. POV: Silas. Emotional beat: doubt poisoning trust.

chapters.title: Confrontation at the River
chapters.summary: Ada admits her connection but swears she learned of the forgery only through Thomas; her real fear is that she'll be next after him. POV: Ada. Emotional beat: vulnerability as strategy and truth.

chapters.title: The Third Witness
chapters.summary: The last living signatory to the deed, elderly Mr. Penhale, agrees to talk — then misses the appointment. Silas finds his cottage searched, the man gone. POV: Silas. Emotional beat: time running out.

chapters.title: Penhale's Hiding Place
chapters.summary: Ada locates Penhale at a care home; he confirms the forgery and names the families, including hers, but refuses to testify out of fear. POV: Ada. Emotional beat: courage borrowed at the last minute.

chapters.title: Midpoint: The Glass Raised Early
chapters.summary: At a parish fundraiser, Fell toasts the community while watching Silas across the room. Two hunters acknowledge each other publicly for the first time. POV: Silas. Emotional beat: open war declared politely.

chapters.title: The Shop Burns
chapters.summary: Arson guts the back room of the bookshop; Silas loses his private case files but realizes the fire spared the front deliberately — a message, not an execution. POV: Silas. Emotional beat: rage sharpening into resolve.

chapters.title: Rebuilding from Memory
chapters.summary: Silas reconstructs his burned files from memory with Ada's help, and in doing so spots the detail he missed nine years ago: Marsh's survey stakes were moved post-mortem. POV: Silas. Emotional beat: grief converted to insight.

chapters.title: Thomas Breaks
chapters.summary: Thomas panics and plans to flee with the deed photos; Ada must choose between letting him run and keeping him as bait for the dinner. POV: Ada. Emotional beat: love against duty, first blood.

chapters.title: The Deacon's Sermon
chapters.summary: Fell preaches on forgiveness and memory, quoting a psalm that mirrors the wording of Marsh's death note — a confession hidden in plain liturgy. POV: Silas. Emotional beat: horror in beautiful packaging.

chapters.title: Alliance of Liars
chapters.summary: Silas, Ada, and Thomas form an uneasy pact: use the anniversary dinner to make Fell confess before witnesses. Each brings a secret they haven't fully shared. POV: rotating. Emotional beat: trust built on mutual leverage.

chapters.title: Rehearsing the Trap
chapters.summary: They plan to swap the authentic deed with a doctored copy that implicates Fell alone, betting his perfectionism will force him to correct the record aloud. POV: Silas. Emotional beat: hope with a blade in it.

chapters.title: The Leak
chapters.summary: Details of the plan surface in Fell's Sunday announcements; someone inside has talked. Suspicion fractures the alliance. POV: Ada. Emotional beat: paranoia's corrosive drip.

chapters.title: Thomas Confesses Everything
chapters.summary: Thomas admits he contacted Fell first, trying to sell silence, which is how Fell learned of the photos. His cowardice nearly doomed them all. POV: Thomas. Emotional beat: shame as reckoning.

chapters.title: Rewriting the Play
chapters.summary: With the original plan burned, Silas designs a new trap around Fell's knowledge: feed him a false version so contaminated that any correction reveals guilt. POV: Silas. Emotional beat: the detective reborn.

chapters.title: Night Before the Dinner
chapters.summary: Quiet interlude: Silas repairs the shop's front window; Ada asks what happens after. An almost-love acknowledged, deferred. POV: alternating. Emotional beat: tenderness on the eve of danger.

chapters.title: The Guest List Closes
chapters.summary: Final preparations: Penhale smuggled in as a 'nurse's companion,' a recorder sewn into a stole, the forged deed placed in the display archive. POV: Ada. Emotional beat: held breath.

chapters.title: The Anniversary Dinner Begins
chapters.summary: Toasts, hymns, the parish's self-congratulation. Fell performs warmth flawlessly while Silas watches his hands. POV: Silas. Emotional beat: elegance stretched over terror.

chapters.title: The Doctored Deed
chapters.summary: The fake deed is unveiled in the anniversary exhibit; Fell's eyes find the altered beneficiary line within seconds. The hook is set. POV: Silas. Emotional beat: predator meeting bait.

chapters.title: Correction, On the Record
chapters.summary: Unable to bear the error, Fell publicly 'corrects' the record with precise details only the forger could know — as Penhale stands and names him. POV: Ada. Emotional beat: triumph curdling into danger.

chapters.title: Climax: The Glass Raised
chapters.summary: Fell, cornered, takes the hall hostage with the truth of everyone's complicity, offering mutual ruin. Silas plays Fell's own recorded sermon confession over the speakers and offers him the choice: arrest or the truth of the first death told fully. Fell lunges; Thomas shields Ada and is wounded but lives. POV: Silas. Emotional beat: everything staked at once.

chapters.title: Aftermath in Broken Glass
chapters.summary: Police arrive to a hall of confessions; Silas hands over everything, including his own nine-year failure. Fell, composed even in cuffs, tells Silas they are the same kind of man. POV: Silas. Emotional beat: victory stained with recognition.

chapters.title: What Love Costs
chapters.summary: Ada faces consequences for concealing her family's benefit from the trust; Silas testifies to her cooperation. Their future is uncertain but chosen honestly. POV: Ada. Emotional beat: love surviving exposure.

chapters.title: The Reopened Ledger
chapters.summary: Weeks later: the shop reopens with new shelves, the parish begins restitution to the trust's rightful heirs, and Penhale's testimony sets precedent. Silas writes his first honest case report. POV: Silas. Emotional beat: quiet restoration.

chapters.title: A Client at Closing Time
chapters.summary: On a rainy evening, a new stranger enters the shop with an impossible request — and Ada, now partner, locks the door behind them. POV: Silas. Emotional beat: the cycle continues, no longer alone.
